title: The Fear of 13 starring Adrien Brody on Broadway #adrienbrody #thefea...
transcript: Like him or not, Adrien Brody is giving a Tony-worthy performance in The Fear of 13. In this documentary-turned-play that marks his Broadway debut, he plays a death row inmate convicted of murder, teetering between hope and hopelessness for an agonizing number of years. When a writer and advocate named Jacki first meets him, he's grown accustomed to his solitude. Over time, however, they form an unexpected connection and he experiences tinges of “real life” in his relationship with her. On paper, the way that things evolve between them isn't something that a lot of people would get behind. In this play, though, the situation is depicted through a remarkably singular and human lens, sufficiently resisting a lot of reservations or judgement. It also helps that Tessa Thompson and Adrien Brody have seemingly effortless chemistry, and the performances across the board are understated but affecting, framed beautifully by the similarly understated yet cold direction by David Cromer. Even if this story doesn't fit your usual taste, Adrien Brody is the real deal. He has these long, distinctive facial features that carry a childlike charisma just as easily as a devastating sorrow. In this production, he doesn't leave the stage for the entire two hours, carrying the show with a delicateness and commitment to the text that's undoubtedly very technical, but flows out of him like a song. I thought he was fantastic, and perhaps my biggest praise for the show is that I didn't check my watch once. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
